The Hang Dau Water Tower, or Tháp nước Hàng Đậu, rises like a giant, cylindrical fortress, its rugged rubble stone and fired brick façade weathered to a moss-tinged gray, as if infused with the patina of time. Built by the French in 1894, this ancient structure was originally designed to supply clean water to the city, its name derived from its location at the head of the street of the same name, which was once renowned for its bustling bean and seed trade.
